name: MINI
intro: MINI originated in United Kingdom. This course teaches selected recognizable model families, organized by the jobs they do. It is a guided starting map, not a claim that these are every current or historical model.
naming: MINI originated in Britain and is part of BMW Group. Cooper, Countryman and Convertible names describe families/bodies whose naming has evolved. ALL4 identifies MINI all-wheel drive; John Cooper Works names performance-related products, not every MINI.
warning: The families below are selected for learning and recognition. Check the linked official range for current Canadian availability, model years, equipment and pricing. A familiar name may remain on used cars after new-car availability changes.

models.name: Cooper 3 Door & 5 Door
models.explanation: MINI Cooper hatchback names include different door configurations. Count the rear hatch when a manufacturer says 3 Door or 5 Door: it is a door too, even though passengers do not normally enter through it.
models.tradeoff: The Cooper 3 Door & 5 Door belongs in a comparison for mini everyday hatchback roles. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare actual rear access, cabin fit and current gas/electric variants. A model name reused across generations does not guarantee identical mechanical systems.
models.scenario: A friend mentions a Cooper 3 Door & 5 Door. Explain its role as mini everyday hatchback roles, then ask for the year, powertrain and equipment before comparing it with another MINI.
models.power: Check the exact Canadian model year and version for the available engine, hybrid or electric system. Do not infer the powertrain from the family name alone.

models.name: Countryman
models.explanation: Countryman is MINI’s SUV family, larger in role than the small hatchback. The name MINI is the brand, not a guarantee that every model is tiny.
models.tradeoff: The Countryman belongs in a comparison for larger mini suv. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare Countryman with Cooper by real exterior dimensions and passenger/cargo fit. ALL4 describes all-wheel drive, not a body style or a universal engine specification.
models.scenario: A friend mentions a Countryman. Explain its role as larger mini suv, then ask for the year, powertrain and equipment before comparing it with another MINI.
models.power: Check the exact Canadian model year and version for the available engine, hybrid or electric system. Do not infer the powertrain from the family name alone.

models.name: MINI Convertible
models.explanation: MINI Convertible is the open-top body role. A roof that opens is the first distinction from a closed hatchback; power and equipment still depend on version.
models.tradeoff: The MINI Convertible belongs in a comparison for mini with an opening roof. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare roof operation, cargo space, passenger fit and intended year-round use with the hatchback. A performance badge does not tell you the roof arrangement.
models.scenario: A friend mentions a MINI Convertible. Explain its role as mini with an opening roof, then ask for the year, powertrain and equipment before comparing it with another MINI.
models.power: Check the exact Canadian model year and version for the available engine, hybrid or electric system. Do not infer the powertrain from the family name alone.
